channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: British Swimmer Completes Strait of Hormuz Swim Amidst Regional Conflict
item.description: British long-distance swimmer and UN Ocean Advocate Lewis Pugh swam approximately 15 kilometers across the Strait of Hormuz over three days. The swim aimed to draw global attention to the environmental damage to marine ecosystems caused by the ongoing conflict. This marks the first such long-distance swim in the Strait since the conflict began in March 2026.

item.title: Court Overturns Release of Former Zhambyl Region Governor Karim Kokrekbayev
item.description: The Almaty Regional Court has overturned a lower court's decision to release former Zhambyl region governor Karim Kokrekbayev from prison due to illness. Prosecutors had appealed the release, stating his condition did not meet the criteria for exemption from serving his sentence.

item.title: Tashkent Police Dismantle Drug Network Involving University Students
item.description: Tashkent law enforcement has busted a drug network that included university students selling synthetic drugs online and via hidden drop-off points. During the operation, police seized significant quantities of mephedrone, MDMA, and cocaine. The network allegedly operated for six months, receiving drugs from abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan hosts discussion on Jordanian King's book promoting peace and dialogue
item.description: The International Institute of Central Asia hosted a roundtable to discuss Jordanian King Abdullah II's book, 'Our Last Best Chance: Building Peace in a Dangerous Time.' The event focused on achieving peace, conflict resolution, and strengthening inter-state relations, with particular attention to the Palestinian-Israeli conflict.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan faces challenges with sanctions, investment, and international reputation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is liquidating 'Processing KG' following UK sanctions. The country faces risks in banking and crypto sectors, threatening foreign investment due to unpredictable procedures and lack of transparency. Additionally, Kyrgyzstan faces issues with migrant document processing in Russia and a widening pension gap between regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman agree on joint projects totaling $5 billion
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have agreed on joint projects worth $5 billion, marking a significant step in strategic partnership between Central Asia and the Gulf Cooperation Council. This collaboration focuses on investment, industrial modernization, energy, transport, and advanced technologies, building on the momentum from the first Central Asia-GCC summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan Clarifies 15% Electricity Prepayment for Businesses
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Regional Electric Networks' clarified that the 15% electricity prepayment benefit applies only to 'exemplary consumers.' Companies must meet criteria like automated metering and no overdue debt. The benefit is automatically granted based on data, not requiring a separate application.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Overturns Early Release of Former Akim Karim Kokirekbaev
item.description: The Almaty Regional Court overturned a decision to release former Akim of Zhambyl region, Karim Kokirekbaev, early due to health reasons. The appellate court found gross violations of legal requirements by the first instance court. Kokirekbaev's condition does not meet the criteria for release.

item.title: Drug Courier with Half a Kilogram of Substance Arrested in Shymkent
item.description: Police in Shymkent arrested a man distributing drugs, who was acting as a courier and packer for an online drug store. Approximately 500 grams of a narcotic substance, considered a large quantity, was found. The suspect used a rented apartment for illegal activities.

item.title: Tashkent Discusses Business Support Measures for Energy Efficiency
item.description: An informational seminar in Tashkent focused on enhancing enterprise energy efficiency, implementing energy-saving technologies, and accessing state financial aid. Organized by the Green Economy Projects Center and the National Energy Efficiency Agency, the event aimed to inform SMEs about government support programs, subsidies, and financial tools for reducing energy consumption. Measures include a 50% compensation for energy audits and interest rate subsidies for loans.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Japan Foreign Ministers Outline Steps for Enhanced Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi met with Japan's Special Representative for Central Asia, Tomoaki Ishigaki, in Astana. They discussed the progress of agreements from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's December 2025 visit to Japan. Discussions also covered prospects for developing trade, economic, and investment cooperation, as well as collaboration within the "Central Asia + Japan" format. Both sides affirmed their interest in strengthening the expanded strategic partnership.

item.title: 13 Convicted Kyrgyz Citizens Transferred from Foreign Prisons to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Thirteen convicted Kyrgyz citizens have been transferred from prisons abroad to Kyrgyzstan following appeals to the president. The Prosecutor General's Office reported that positive decisions were made on 13 out of 21 received appeals, with four applicants being denied.

item.title: Ukraine Confirms Attack on Russian Ships in Libyan Waters
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian security forces attacked a Russian military ship and a cargo ship in Libyan waters. The attack, using seven naval drones, reportedly sank the Russian military vessel 'Mercury'. The Kremlin has stated the Ministry of Defense will provide further details.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Security Chief Admits Violations in Property Repatriation
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNБ), Maksat Asanaliev, has acknowledged that violations occurred during the process of returning property to state ownership as part of anti-corruption efforts. He stated that the GKNБ is taking measures to prevent similar situations in the future.

item.title: Tajikistan Officially Notifies UN of Withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: Tajikistan has officially informed the UN of its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC). The withdrawal will take effect on November 20, 2027, one year after the notification. The country had signed the Rome Statute in 1998 and ratified it in 2000.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry and AIFC Collaborate to Attract Investors
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) have launched an investment dialogue to promote investment opportunities and attract foreign investors. The event, attended by diplomatic corps and international organizations, highlighted Kazakhstan's growing role as a regional investment hub and its commitment to economic diplomacy.

item.title: Tajikistan Officially Notifies UN of Withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has officially informed the United Nations of its withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC). The withdrawal will become effective on November 20, 2027, one year after the notification. Tajikistan is the fourth country to begin the formal withdrawal process since the US called for dismantling the court.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Activist's Lawyers Withdraw from Court Hearing
item.description: Lawyers for activist Sanzhar Bokayev withdrew from a court hearing on November 23 after their request to express distrust in the court was denied. This decision followed the judge's repeated rejection of their motion. Earlier, prosecutors requested that witness Ahliiddin Khamrakulov's testimony be removed from case materials.

item.title: Nvidia Founder Jensen Huang Reinstated as CEO After 11-Day Absence
item.description: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, 11 days after his resignation. The board, initially opposed to his return, reversed its decision after negotiations and consultations with senior US officials. The board unanimously voted to reinstate Huang, citing no national security threat. His return boosted Nvidia's stock by over 31%.

item.title: Afghan Traders in Delhi Face Challenges Due to High Transport Costs
item.description: Afghan traders at an international trade fair in Delhi are struggling with high transport costs, making it difficult to compete. Haji Shah Agha noted that air freight costs $1.55 per kilogram, significantly increasing product prices. He stated that ground transport would be cheaper and improve sales, as lower prices attract more buyers.

item.title: Afghanistan's Central Bank to Auction $16 Million Amid Rising Dollar Rates
item.description: Afghanistan's Central Bank, now under Taliban control, announced it will auction $16 million USD on Tuesday. This move comes as the dollar's exchange rate against the Afghani has risen, with one dollar reaching over 66.50 Afghani. The bank has invited banks and money exchange companies to participate in the auction aimed at stabilizing currency rates.

item.title: Uzbek Labor Migrants Seek New Opportunities in Europe as Russia Becomes Less Viable
item.description: For years, Russia was the primary destination for Uzbek labor migrants. However, due to the war, increased raids, and new restrictions, many are now seeking alternative paths. This report explores the challenges and opportunities faced by Uzbek citizens moving to Europe, which offers better prospects but also presents its own difficulties. Can Europe become the next choice after Russia?

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces Natural Gas Shortages Ahead of Winter Amid Declining Production
item.description: Uzbekistan is experiencing significant natural gas supply issues even before winter's arrival, with widespread disruptions in Tashkent and restrictions on gas filling stations in regions. Gas production decreased by 16.4% in January-September 2026 compared to the previous year, while domestic consumption continues to rise, exacerbating the deficit.

item.title: Russian Forces Attack Ukrainian Regions, Missile Hits Poland
item.description: Russian forces launched attacks across several Ukrainian regions. In the Kyiv region, a strike on a store in Bucha killed at least three people. In Dymer, a child was rescued from the rubble of a residential building destroyed by an air strike, with 11 deaths reported. Two Russian ships exploded in the port of Benghazi, Libya.

item.title: China's Xi Jinping Strengthens Position After Meetings with Trump and Putin
item.description: US President Donald Trump called his visit to China a diplomatic victory. However, analysts suggest that three meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping this year have not yielded significant results for Washington. Beijing stated it made no new substantial concessions on key US demands, gaining maneuvering room on Taiwan and tech embargo issues.

item.title: Jordan Prepares to Sign Trade Agreement and Host Business Forum with Uzbekistan
item.description: Jordan is preparing to sign a preferential trade agreement and host a business forum with Uzbekistan. These events will take place during Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit. Officials discussed final preparations, emphasizing the visit's importance for bilateral economic ties. Priority areas include pharmaceuticals, food processing, chemicals, textiles, mining, fertilizers, energy, transport, and logistics.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan Prepare to Sign Preferential Trade Agreement
item.description: Jordan is preparing to sign a preferential trade agreement with Uzbekistan and host a business forum. This will occur during Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit. Ministers discussed final preparations, emphasizing the visit's importance for bilateral relations and economic cooperation in sectors like pharmaceuticals, energy, and logistics.

item.title: Reconstruction of Major Road Completed in Kazakhstan's Ulytau Region
item.description: The reconstruction of the Kyzylorda-Zhezkazgan highway section in Kazakhstan's Ulytau region is complete, finalizing the 400 km road upgrade. The project involved laying 1.3 million tons of asphalt, building bridges, and installing culverts and animal crossings. The improved road will enhance regional transport links and socio-economic development.

item.title: Interview: Andrea Zinzani on Central Asia's Environmental Governance Challenges
item.description: Geographer Andrea Zinzani discusses environmental policies in Central Asia, focusing on water governance and climate adaptation. He highlights the exclusion of local communities from decision-making and the tensions between conservation, economic development, and community interests. Zinzani emphasizes the need to examine political and institutional dynamics shaping environmental governance beyond physical consequences.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Signs Decree on Developing National Digital Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree aimed at developing the national digital economy and expanding economic opportunities for citizens and businesses. The document focuses on developing digital employment, applying artificial intelligence, and expanding the market for domestic products. The government must approve a comprehensive plan for developing the national digital economy by December 1, 2026.

item.title: Violence in Kazakhstan's education system is a systemic problem, not isolated incidents
item.description: Recent tragic events at KazNU highlight systemic societal issues in Kazakhstan, where violence is used as a problem-solving tool. This is evident in violence against children, between genders, and among peers, particularly in institutions like education and the military, where physical strength dictates leadership. The article points to a pervasive culture of violence impacting schools and universities across the country.

item.title: Armenian Prime Minister Unveils Draft of New Constitution
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has announced the draft of a new constitution, available online for public review and feedback. The draft omits a reference to the 1990 Declaration of Independence and mentions the 1991 resolution on the "Reunification of" Nagorno-Karabakh. This omission is a condition set by Azerbaijan for signing a peace treaty.

item.title: Man Arrested in Uzgen for Suspected Home Drug Possession
item.description: A man has been detained in Uzgen on suspicion of possessing drugs at his home. Authorities have initiated a criminal case under the article 'Illegal production of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, and their analogues without the intent to sell.' Approximately 1.885 kilograms of marijuana were seized from his residence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tax System Reforms: Key Changes for Businesses and Citizens Over Five Years
item.description: Over the past five years, Kyrgyzstan's tax system has undergone significant changes, including zero rates for small businesses, abolition of the transport tax, and expansion of tax benefits. Tax revenues have nearly tripled. Most services are now electronic, with over 1.7 million users of online services, simplifying tax procedures for businesses and citizens.

item.title: Four Kazakh Citizens Injured in Traffic Accident in Oman, MFA Reports
item.description: Four Kazakh citizens from the same family were injured in a road traffic accident in Salalah, Oman. Kazakh diplomats are providing consular assistance and are in contact with doctors. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is handling the issue of their return to Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Decree on People's Digital Economy Development
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree to develop Kazakhstan's people's digital economy. The initiative aims to transform the labor market and e-commerce, simplify legal frameworks for platform employment, and connect rural producers to marketplaces. Recommendations from AI expert Li Kaifu on practical AI skills training are to be incorporated.

item.title: Meta Disables Facebook Accounts of Kazakh Journalists Alleging 'Death'
item.description: Meta has disabled the Facebook accounts of several Kazakh journalists, including Irina Petrushova, Natalia Sadykova, and Dinara Egeubaeva, by marking them as deceased. The journalists allege this is a new pressure tactic by Kazakh authorities following investigations into the National Security Committee. They claim fake death certificates were sent to Meta.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches People's Digital Economy Initiative
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree on developing a people's digital economy in Kazakhstan. The government must approve a comprehensive plan by December 1, regulating digital employment and expanding opportunities for the self-employed and rural entrepreneurs by year-end. The plan aims to increase citizen incomes and support businesses through digital employment and AI.

item.title: European Natural Gas Prices Spike Ahead of Winter Season
item.description: Natural gas prices in European countries surged by 8.6% in one day, reaching 96 euros per megawatt-hour. Insufficient preparation of reserves for winter also contributed to the price increase. The situation highlights concerns about energy supply stability.

item.title: Trial Begins for Former State Security Officials in Closed Hearing
item.description: A trial has commenced for Eldar Jakypbekov and Sydyk Duyshomiyev, former employees of the State Committee for National Security and associates of its ex-chairman Kamchybek Tashiev. The proceedings are being held behind closed doors due to a "secret" classification of the criminal case. Details remain undisclosed.
